briefs.title: Video Use MCP
briefs.description: A product film showing the reference-to-preview workflow inside a conversation.
briefs.promptSource: Original Video Use product film; the open-source launch-title prompt is a structural starting point only.
briefs.prompt: Create a 24-second 1920×1080 launch film for Video Use MCP using the current Video Use production workflow. Match the actual Video Use website: soft lavender, warm near-white, dark ink, generous space, a refined serif headline paired with clear sans-serif UI text. Use the real Video Use mark from this repository. Open with the promise “Your idea. A video worth making.” A generic chat interface receives the brief “Make a launch video for my new note-taking app.” At 4 seconds, show three compact reference cards with original abstract thumbnails; one is selected. The selected composition opens up while its old copy changes to the fictional product name “Fieldnote” and a note-card interface, visually demonstrating adaptation. At 11 seconds, show a short playable snippet preview with the controls “Refine” and “Continue”. Let the pointer select Continue only after the snippet has been shown. At 17 seconds, reveal the completed Fieldnote launch video beside its editable project/source card and an MP4 download action. End with the real Video Use mark and “Create in your conversation”, followed by small plain text “ChatGPT · Claude”. The film should explain this sequence through actions and clean camera framing, with no long setup checklist. Use a recurring moving lavender cursor or line to carry attention between the chat, reference, preview and result. Keep each UI state readable, the ending visible for 3 seconds, and the film understandable muted for website autoplay. Sound can be a very quiet original pulse and UI accents. Avoid invented testimonials, prices, usage statistics, provider endorsements, guarantees of universal MCP support, and photorealistic image/video generation claims. Deliver the finished MP4, an autoplay-friendly compressed copy, a poster, and editable scene source. Review rendered frames and the full transition sequence before delivery.
briefs.assetPlan: Use the repository’s actual logo and site font/color tokens. Create fictional source thumbnails, Fieldnote UI, generic chat layout and result preview from original vector/code assets. Reuse an actual verified showcase render as the final in-video result if available, with permission/source tracked; otherwise render the small fictional Fieldnote scene as part of this job.

briefs.prompt: Use Video Use to make a 26-second 1920×1080 classroom explainer answering “Which is larger: 2/3 or 3/4?” Draw two exactly equal-length horizontal bars. Then subdivide both into twelfths without changing their widths: 2/3 becomes 8/12 and 3/4 becomes 9/12. Isolate the single extra twelfth in warm coral and end on “3/4 is larger by 1/12”. Use gentle line drawing and precise label placement; leave the final annotated comparison visible for 4 seconds. No voiceover is needed because each step is visibly explained.
